It is forwarding this same telegram, dated the 1st, to Bosanski Brod, Srpska Krupa, Drvar, Glamoc, Bosansko Grahovo, Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Serbian Station, et cetera, Boskoski Petrovac, also. Does this correspond to what was sent from the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the chief of the Security Centre acted on instructions from that dispatch from the 31st of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a customary method of dealing with such things?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D391, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here: "The transformation of the Centre of Security Services, it has been concluded, has not been done on a mono-national basis, and we shall not allow the one party taking of facilities and equipment. The workers shall voluntarily opt, provided that under the new Law on the Interior, everybody has been given the opportunity to remain working at the posts at which they were when the transformation was undertaken." Mr. Minister, you were quite well versed in the goings-on in the judiciary, et cetera, when, for instance, the Serbian municipality of Krupa and the Muslim municipality of Krupa were to merge. We can see, on the basis of this document, that the police stations will not necessarily be mono-national?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is according to the Law on Internal Affairs, and according to my dispatch, and according to the Constitution of the Republika Srpska, where it is stated that whosoever wished to remain working in that centre could do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this reflected, in a proportionate way, the share of that respective people in the Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the place concerned where a municipality or a police station was to be set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The rest of the police of Muslim ethnicity who lived in a newly-formed Muslim municipality were supposed to join their newly-established police station; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in the realm of probability. I cannot say anything specific. Probably. People actually go to work where they are assigned to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any tensions or was there potential for tensions? If, in those times, a purely Muslim patrol would go to a Serbian village or neighbourhood, and vice versa, was that a quite risky exercise?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in some municipalities, even in the absence of a political recommendation, I think in Ilidza, Tomo Kovac and his colleague from Hrasnica agreed informally that that Muslim policemen should be sent to Hrasnica and Serbian policemen to the Serbian part of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As there were inter-ethnic tensions, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted? It has been admitted. All right, thank you. Can we now see 1D1907.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the 4th of April, without the consent of the Serbian representative, Professor Koljevic and Professoresse [as interpreted] Plavsic, had adopted a decision on general mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this so-called rump Presidency without the Serbian representatives sat daily from the 4th until the 8th of April, when the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina was proclaimed on the basis of the recognition of it by the European Union on the 6th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, Mr. Minister, that the Presidency undertook upon itself that the referendum results would not prejudge the political order and system of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that that had been concluded and accepted on the 2nd of March at a session together with Mr. Dukic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had occasion to see that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that since the decisions of the people -- that the people's decision at the referendum was never verified at the session of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as required under the Constitution?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the Constitution, to change the social order of the republic, two-thirds of the population should have voted in favour of that. That is 66 point something per cent. According to the results published by the two sides, the out-turn at the referendum had been 64 per cent of the population, so that that legal provision was not met and the referendum could, therefore, not have been constitutionally legal, even though one constituent people completely disregarded the referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the two-thirds requirement was not met for the referendum. But do you agree that in any scenario, it should have been verified, I mean, the results of the referendum should have been verified at the Assembly session by the Assembly and proclaimed by also a two-thirds majority of all the MPs?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a constitutional category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that that could not have been adopted in the Assembly because of the 86 Serbs -- at least 83 of the Serb MPs in the Assembly would have voted against, and maybe more?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know what would have happened had that been the case, but I do know that it had not been tabled on the agenda of the Assembly for verification and that the Assembly did not function, in fact, at that time at all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the second page now. In English, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you interpret for us or read these points out for us of the decision of the 4th of April, namely?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Presidency of the SR BH, at its session held today on the 4th of April, 1992, bearing in mind the complexity of the political and security situation in the republic, concluded: "1. That in keeping with the decision of the SR BH Presidency of the 3rd of April, 1992, and its own assessment, a mobilisation be carried out of the territorial defence units of all the municipalities and the city of Sarajevo in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including communications units. "2. That it will demand from the responsible organs of the Yugoslav People's Army that the weapons, military equipment and other materiel and technical equipment that were entrusted to them for safekeeping be returned to territorial defence units - municipal and district BH TO staffs. "3. That a mobilisation be carried out of the entire reserve force of the SR BH police, in keeping with the earlier decisions of the Presidency and Government of the SR BH."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope the parties can see the rest. Let's just remind ourselves. The entire Territorial Defence is raised, mobilised. Do you remember that according to our Law on All People's Defence and People's Self-Protection, it is the president of the municipality who commands the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the level of the republic, it's the Council of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's according to that law we cited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that before this mobilisation, an unlawful increase was made to the reserve police force, up to 100 per cent, up to 600, by taking over the unassigned military conscripts, Croats and Muslims, who had not responded to JNA mobilisation call?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that Sefer Halilovic, up to this date, had already created 103 municipal staffs and 9 regional staffs, with over 100.000 or 150.000 members of the Patriotic League, plus various paramilitary formations, Green Berets and such, is this really, by now, a respectable military force with close to 300.000 men?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sefer Halilovic, an active-duty JNA officer, in the summer of 1991 began to establish and established paramilitary formations called the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In this decision, they didn't state it, but do you remember that the Serbian part of the Presidency disputed this mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the Serbian members of the Presidency did not participate in these conclusions. And what they may have disputed later, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your view, as the boss of all crime prevention services in all of Bosnia, was this a frightening decision for the entire Serbian people? In addition to being illegal, in addition to the Serbian veto, was it really frightening in its scope and implications?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find the right words to explain this now, but it was obvious that Bosnia and Herzegovina was collapsing as a result of all these events, and there was no understanding to be found between members of the government and the Presidency. And under partisan pressure and by importing people from other countries, they tore up the MUP. And I mean the Party of Democratic Action did it, not my dispatch or all the other things quoted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was the supposed enemy of this major force?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D392, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D1914. It's minutes of this protracted Presidency session from April 4 to 8. We also have a translation. The 4th, 5th, 6th, and the 8th of April, the Presidency sat. Nikola Koljevic and Biljana Plavsic were absent, and on the agenda, we see the first fight and the political insecurity situation. Can we move to page 2 in both version. We've heard all this before. The Civilian Protection and the entire police force are being mobilised and activated. Can we see page 3 in English and page 4 in Serbian. This would be from the session of the 8th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, the Presidency held the fourth round of its session, considering the difficult political and security situation, before adopting the following decisions. And we can move to page 4 in English. And here we see the proclamation of imminent threat of war. The republic was renamed from "Socialist Republic" into just "Republic." The hitherto Republic Staff of Territorial Defence is abolished, and the Staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina is established. This is a total break with all the institutions that had existed until then?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 5 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They decide that the use of the Territorial Defence would be a matter for the Presidency of the republic to decide. The Ministry of Defence would, through the Staff of Territorial Defence, command and control TO units. And further below, it says the Presidency relieved from duty commander of the republic and Territorial Defence Staff of BH and the chief of the Republic Territorial Defence Staff, Drago Vukosavljevic, a Serb, and Fikret Jahic, a Muslim, respectively, and instead they appointed Colonel Hasan Efendic, commander of the Territorial Defence Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Colonel Stjepan Siber, chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence. Do you remember that Hasan Efendic became the commander, the top position, in the Territorial Defence Staff?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that four days later, the same Hasan Efendic issued a directive to mount obstacles put, put up hindrances, and otherwise harass the JNA Army in the entire territory?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasan Efendic proclaimed the JNA to be an enemy of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He issued an order to mount obstacles on the roads, to seize JNA weapons, and all the rest that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this moment marked the collapse -- the complete breakdown of the system in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destruction had started before, and this was just the final moment of collapse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We've seen a document before in which your then Minister Delimustafic voices his critique at the session of the Presidency and says, What are you doing? You proclaimed war on the JNA. That's what he had to say about these instructions issued by Hasan Efendic to undertake military action against the JNA, which at that moment was still the military -- the legal military force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in all the barracks and garrisons throughout the republic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 65 ter 05878. 05878. We believe it has a translation. It's a Prosecution document. This is a communique of the National Defence Council, which is an advisory body to the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this National Security Council has been in existence for seven days at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read the first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Public Announcement": "The rump Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, operating without any representatives of the Serbian people, has issued highly irresponsible and illegal instructions regarding the activation of Territorial Defence and people's self-organisation, and the activation of Civilian Protection and reserve police."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Go on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With this move, the rump Presidency --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not find this.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Presidency has acknowledged the collapse of the constitutional and legal order, as well as that of legal authorities and has thus instigated chaos, violence and civil war. "The Serbian National Defence Council appeals to the people to ignore this --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page. Please go on, Mr. Mandic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The Serbian National Security Council hereby calls upon the people to disregard this ill-advised appeal of the rump BH Presidency and do everything in its power to avoid civil war and the suffering of the people."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you finish, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Serb National Defence Council hereby orders that should any Territorial Defence, Civilian Protection or reserve police units in any area respond to this invitation of the Presidency, crisis staffs in those areas should be activated and the Serbian people's Territorial Defence, Civilian Protection and reserve police mobilised, primarily for the purpose of maintaining the order, peace, and safety of civilians of all nationalities. "President of the council, Dr. Radovan Karadzic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that they had activated their own crisis staffs already in the summer of 1992 -- sorry, summer of 1991, and the Serbs did that only just before the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the control of Sefer Halilovic and the Patriotic League, staffs had already been created in municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If this document is true and the admission of Sefer Halilovic is true, that there were staffs and units already created in 110 municipalities, would that mean that they were not created only in Croat municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in these 103 municipalities, there was a significant share of the Serbian population, and in 40 of them there was even an absolute Serbian majority?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be positive about any numbers or municipalities with a majority Serbian population, but I know that quite a few of the 109 had a majority Serbian population, such as in Eastern Herzegovina, a part of Posavina, the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in all these activities to establish an illegal army, the local Serbian population could see exactly what it was all about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D394, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D170.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You adopted into evidence the request of Sefer Halilovic to be promoted, where he says that already in September 1991, he had already created 98 of these staffs, and now we see what this plan of preparations and organisation of the Patriotic League for the defence of the sovereign Republic of BH looks like. Just read the sub-headlines. Do we have a translation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just read the headings.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Preparation and Organisation of the Patriotic League to Defend the Sovereign Republic of BH." Heading 1: "Main Political Staff of the Patriotic League." "Composition." "Task." "Regional/Political Staff of the Patriotic League."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we scroll down?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Municipal/Political Staff of the Patriotic League." "Main Military Staff of the Patriotic League, BH."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page, please. Just the headings.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already read this. We need the rest of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we then see page 3. No, these are military staffs. You were reading about the political staffs, but I can do it instead of you. "Regional Military Staff" and "Municipal Military Staff." So they had a political line and a military line. Can you read about the tasks?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Task of Sector Units." "Tasks of Manoeuvring Units." "Tasks of Logistical Units."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last page, please. Just the underlined bit.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the level of municipalities, establish municipal logistical bases," and the same on the regional level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this a criminal activity in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a paramilitary formation, it was the establishment of a para-army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you, in the police, aware of this activity?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D395, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 1D1093, please, could we have that. 1D1093. Could we just see the number? Yes, well, that's it, right. Now we have the translation, too. Could we please have page 2 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, is this an announcement of the Serbian minister -- rather, the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sarajevo? The date is the 5th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, can you read this out: "In light of the events of last night and today, in Sarajevo, the Ministry of Internal Affairs in the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is issuing the following announcement ..." This has to do with mobilisation, or, rather, what happened in Sarajevo immediately on the evening of the 4th after the mobilisation had been declared; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Announcement." "On the 4th of April, 1992, at around 2300 hours, intensive preparations were commenced by the Muslim part of the former Ministry of Internal Affairs for the blocking and overtaking of the Ministry of Internal Affairs building, as well as the Krtelji landmark, where the special unit were stationed. Following the forced taking of the ministry building and the expulsion of ministry employees of Serb nationality or ethnicity, an intense attack was carried out on the Krtelji landmark, via a runway of the Sarajevo Airport, which had already been taken by the aforementioned units and the so-called Green Berets."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope that we can skip part of it. Everyone can rea, I hope. Can you then go on from this action? Actually, Novo Sarajevo, what happened in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it the same page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same paragraph: "Somewhat later, around 1.00, to be more precise ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sometime later, at around 1.00, a classical terrorist attack was carried out by the so-called Green Berets, in which the Public Security Station of Novo Sarajevo was taken. During that attack, police officer Pero Petrovic was killed, while two other police officers on duty were disarmed and taken prisoner. In this operation, the Green Berets, the complete arsenal of weapons and equipment were taken and distributed to citizens of Muslim ethnicity. Simultaneously, the Green Berets, along with the active and reserve police formations of Muslim ethnicity, had usurped practically all vital facilities in the city of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree, Minister, that that night, a few hours after general mobilisation was declared, the Green Berets carried out this terror in Sarajevo and that there was practically not a single building left that they had not taken with their sniper shooters?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you the following -- actually, can this document be admitted? I would like to ask you about what happened with the special unit that, in accordance with the current process of agreement-reaching and the establishment of the two police forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina -- actually, it was divided on the basis of this agreement on the 4th of April into two police units -- police forces, rather. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D396, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Mr. Minister, if I say that in the special unit, and it was used unlawfully, and Delimustafic speaks about that during his testimony in Sarajevo, weren't there objections in this regard throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina? So am I right when I say that on the 4th of April, in the evening, they reached an agreement and parted in a friendly way, they embraced and kissed, and they said, You take this much equipment, we'll take that much, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was preceded by the nucleus of the collegium of the minister at the base of the special unit in Krtelji, attended by Vito Zepinic, Jusuf Pusina, and Bruno Stojic. We know that the commander of the special unit was Dragan Vikic, a very honest and capable policeman, a Croat, and it was agreed then, and on orders issued by the minister, that the Serb part of the unit be relocated to the special unit facility that was at the school in Vrace, the so-called F facility, whereas the second part of the special unit, consisting of Muslims and Croats, should go to the police centre at Bjelave. That was the order of Minister Delimustafic that was carried out by these three assistant ministers, and that is when this peaceful parting took place among people who had already clashed. On that occasion, the members of the special unit, who had been trained for anti-terrorist activity, hostage crises, dealing with natural disasters, et cetera, left that facility carrying their personal weapons only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was expected --

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. That is what was confirmed by Mr. Delimustafic when he testified in my case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the SDA try to undermine this agreement on the peaceful split of the special unit, and did they try to talk the Serbian members to stay on?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Attempts were made through Mr. Zepinic to recruit - let me think - Miodrag Repija and Dragimir Maric. They offered apartments to them if they were to stay on, but that was after the agreement was reached and after the meeting took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next week, we are going to present some documents that speak about these attempts. Do we agree that on the next day, the police, the Serb police -- actually, the Serb part of the special unit, when they were moving into the premises provided to them, came across an ambush, and two Serb policemen got killed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the special unit parted on the 4th of April. Facility F, that was the headquarters of the special unit, had not been used for several years, and it had been agreed that it would be cleaned and that the members of the special units would then enter before the political disagreements were resolved. They spent that night at the facility in Blazuj. I think that it belonged to the UPI economic organisation. When it was reported that the facility had been prepared for taking these people in, they went there, carrying their own weapons. And in front of this facility, they were met by 170 men in trenches. They were armed, and they opened fire at them. On that occasion, two Serbs were killed, Pupic and Lizdek. They were members of the special unit. Three were wounded, Jevic, Dusko, and Repija, Miodrag, and I don't know the name of the third one. And eight civilians got killed, too, who lived nearby. They were killed in their apartments; also a man who had a kiosk there. On that occasion, of course, there weren't any casualties on the side of those who had staged the ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That Serb special unit, was it intended in the first place for anti-sabotage activities, natural disasters, and so on? Was the Serb part supposed to be in Serb neighbourhoods, and the Muslim part in Muslim neighbourhoods, in order to avoid any tension?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the agreement that was agreed upon -- that was reached only recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serb specials managed to overcome and -- these 170 trained men and also save the lives of the cadets without having any casualties?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Some mention has been made of some assistance that came from a tank unit of the JNA in Lukavica. Do you remember that that tank unit at that point in time was commanded by Colonel Enver Hadzihasanovic, later an officer of the Muslim Army?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know with certainty that the armed members of the paramilitary formations, the Patriotic League and the Green Berets, moved from the Vrace monument into a new clash with the Serb specials and the police that had already been stationed there at the school. Then, at the request -- the public call made by Mr. Izetbegovic, the army went out to separate the two sides. Had that not been done, there would have been an armed conflict of an even larger scale and there would have been more casualties. The army did not fire a single bullet. They went out, they separated the warring parties -- or, actually, not warring parties. The war had not started yet. The two parties in this conflict. And then these men withdrew, at the request of Avdo Hebib, not to clash with the army and the Serb police, and they returned, via Kovaci, down there to Grbavica, to the centre of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have in e-court 1D1906. While we're waiting for that -- well, yes, we have the first page here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, let me familiarise you with this. This is a document of the minister of defence of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. On the 5th of April, before the recognition of Bosnia-Herzegovina, he took over powers that were somewhat more extensive than those envisaged by law, since defence fell under the jurisdiction of the federal state?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, defence fell under the jurisdiction of the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here it is, then. He is writing to all the presidents of municipalities, of executive councils, municipal secretariats for national defence, town secretariats for national defence, assistant minister for national defence in the district, and the commander of the Republican Territorial Defence Staff. He says here on the first page: "Assess the need to mobilise certain units of the Territorial Defence." Can we now move on to the next page in Serbian. English, too, actually, next page. I'm afraid that you cannot see these conclusions, so I'll read it out, and the English is quite legible: "1. The Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina calls on all citizens, as well as state organs and political parties, to focus all their efforts on maintaining peace," et cetera. Then paragraph 2: "The Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina charges the BH Ministry of National Defence to immediately provide expert assistance to those municipalities which assess that there is a need for mobilisation and to secure the materiel and technical equipment required," et cetera, et cetera. Perhaps you cannot see this in the Serbian version, but then it also says: "Appropriate weapons to units of the Territorial Defence that are indispensable." That is what is supposed to be secured, that is. So the minister of defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina is being charged to provide necessary weapons and equipment to units of the Territorial Defence that is indispensable for ensuring public law and order and securing vital facilities, and instructing and co-ordinating compulsory activities of the subjects of the Territorial Defence, and so on and so forth. Next page, please. Have you heard of this? Did you know about this telegram, sent by Minister Jerko Doko, that was actually an instruction for the melding of the police and the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I was not aware of this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this look like a take-over of the powers of the federal state?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This melding or merging of the Territorial Defence, what does it look like to you? Does it look like a public and open establishment of an armed force of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, apart from the Patriotic League and other paramilitaries? Now the joint armed units are becoming the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This meant placing under a single command all the armed forces that were in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Although you're not familiar with this document, you are familiar with the phenomenon, itself; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we saw that on the basis of the previous documents and communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that sometime on the 15th of April, they established this Territorial Defence officially, and somewhat later they declared this to be the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D397, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 1D18888 in e-court, please. 1D1888. This is a telegram. I don't know whether we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you tell the Chamber and the parties what this is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a telegram by the chief of the centre in Doboj, the chief of the Security Services in Doboj, Andrija Bjelosevic, and he says: "As chief of the Security Services in Doboj, I have to draw your attention to the fact that measures of preparedness of the first and second degree are to be taken upon the proclamation of extraordinary circumstances, i.e., those from the third degree upon the proclamation of war, state of war, which is in the competence of the Presidency of the SFRY according to the valid regulations. "In addition to that, by your document DT number 08147 of the 2nd of November, 1990, the MUP receives and passes on the ordered measures of alert, but does not issue any orders to that effect, itself."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you like to explain to us what was this chief from Doboj writing to the MUP and to the federal SUP? What were the illegalities he had noticed? What was he talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proclamation of the first- and second-level measures, and he insisted on the MUP only being empowered to transmit orders, rather to issue them, themselves; that they had arrogated upon themselves some powers which were within the competence of the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the 6th of April. So after having received all these measures that had been taken by Doko and by the government and by the rump Presidency, he observed these illegal practices and informed thereon the MUP and the federal secretariat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D398, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it is possible for me to clarify one document before the break. This is a document I would like to call, it is 1D855. We ought to have the translation. We probably do so if we could see both versions, the Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, this is from your jurisdiction. 1D855 is the number. This is from within your sphere of competence. This is general crime. This is the examination of Senad Memic, Senad Memic, born in 1953, and the interrogation took place on the 14th of April, 1992. Are you aware of this arrest and this interrogation?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aren't these those lads who were captured -- who were arrested on Mount Igman or Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see, in the first paragraph they were arms dealers who had distributed around 5.000 automatic rifles, and so on. Do you see this first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You do not have, in the Serbian version: "In the period from September ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please read this document and then tell us what it is about? They refer to the Muslim part of the MUP, Jusuf Pusina, Bakir Alispahic, Kemal Sabovic, Mirsad Srebrenkovic. Kemal Sabovic who replaced Stanisic, who had been removed; then Alibabic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we get into this document, I want to raise an objection to it. I'll start with the simplest one, the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wanted to ask the accused as to its foundation. That's the concern?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's the first one, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't see the author, and we have no clue what this is about, so could you clarify that first, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, was this a customary dispatch in communication in the MUP, in the police of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Was this a standard telex by which such communication was carried out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the accused is focusing on the previous telex by Mr. Bjelosevic. The concern at the moment was the document currently on screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, this is also pertinent to this. This is a standard-model document, so I would like to know whether the minister recognises this standard form of communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's see whether Mr. Mandic can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a statement taken from this person by the authorised official in the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How can we know this, seeing this document, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was in this way that policemen took statements from any interrogated persons. You will see that it bears a signature. I don't see it now, but it is certainly there. In the right corner is the signature of the authorised policeman, police official, and in the left corner, of the person who gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Collapse the English for the moment and let's see the entire document, first page. Can we see the entire document in one page, without zooming in, whether there's any signature. And can we go to the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the handwriting of the arrested Senad Memic. This is his statement, in his own hand. It was forwarded by telefax.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does this one have a signature, Mr. President, the handwritten one? It has to have a signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see page 4 of this. Can you tell us whether it has some signature, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not see a signature on this page. There has to be more text, I expect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There have to be many more pages, many more handwritten pages, because in the telex there are two and a half typewritten pages. So if we could look through the handwritten statement, we would -- we could find the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is only 10 pages, so we can start from that first page and we can go through until page 10. Take a brief look, Mr. Mandic. No, we start from page 1, and show page 2, page 3, page 4, and continue until page 10. This is the last page of the typed version. I see no name. And we'll continue to the handwritten part. It continues in that way. Now, you have seen the entire document, so what can you tell us about this document, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll up the last page to see the end of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the B/C/S, can we see the end of the page, scroll it up. A bit more, a bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just want it scrolled up -- or, rather, down. We want to see the end of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think this is the whole document, as we have it. And I also have to note that page 8 and 9 in the handwritten part are missing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to me, Your Honours, that this is not the complete document. Evidently, the handwritten statement of one Memic from Hrasnica was typewritten, but it should have had -- the handwritten statement should bear the signature of the person giving, and the statement and the typewritten version should have the signature of the person who typed it. So it does seem to me that this document is incomplete.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall try to search the EDS to have it completed, and for the time being I can and shall withdraw it. Is it, Your Honours, time for our break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break for an hour. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Over the break, Mr. Tieger and Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber had the opportunity to discuss the issue regarding the transcript, in the Bosnian part. According to the guide-line we gave, the Chamber will not admit the transcript of the other tribunal or in foreign countries, but the Chamber sees no problem putting the question to the witness, who was there at the time. So we'll allow you to continue putting your question. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is quite acceptable to the Defence. Can we call up, please, 1D1908, to jog Mr. Mandic's memory, very briefly. Just a few questions. Page 7 in Serbian; page 6 in English. MR. KARADZIC [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are the pages. We've discussed this. Defence Counsel Serdarevic asks about the barricades after the killing of the member of the wedding party in Bascarsija, and Mr. Delimustafic says it was our duty to deblock the town and that you were sent on behalf of the ministry to get them to do this. And Mr. Serdarevic says: "Would you tell us who had set up the barricades?" And Mr. Delimustafic says: "Well, these people who were dissatisfied about this killing of the member of the wedding party." And then he says: "It was the Serbs."

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was sent by the collegium of the ministry to inspect these barricades to avoid a major disturbance of law and order, because Mr. Delimustafic had ordered this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did it ever cross our minds that the barricades had been set up because of the referendum, or were they set up because of that killing of the member of the wedding party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no doubt in anyone's mind that it was all done over the killing of the bride's father in Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that the killer was treated as a hero and that he appeared very soon on television to explain why he had killed that member of the wedding party?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was invited to a TV show.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The parties can read this, but this is the passage that I wanted to go on the record. Serbian page 8 now, and English page 7. The question was: "As far as Vraca is concerned, Mr. Minister, did you know that the Serb part of the special unit would go to the F building at Vraca?" And Delimustafic's answer was: "Well, Vito informed us at the collegium, since he had been a couple of times at meetings at Krtelji, where the unit's base was, that they had agreed to split up peacefully, and that the Serb part of this unit would move to Vraca." And then your question: "Do you know that two Serb special policemen were killed and three wounded at Vraca? Were you informed about it?" Mr. Delimustafic says: "I think so. I think I heard that it had happened." Then the next question: "Do you know that none of the students or the personnel was either wounded or hurt during that conflict ..." And Delimustafic says: "I do." And then the Accused Mandic says: "If we had stayed together, you had worked in the police force for a long time, we co-operated, and I assumed the office at your and Vito Zepinic's proposal, I mean, you proposed it to the SDS ..." And Delimustafic corrects you and say: "To Rajko Dukic." And then the question goes on: "If we had stayed together, whom would you have considered as responsible for the conflict at Vraca? Who placed -- provoked the conflict without your approval?" And then we have his answer on Serbian page 9 and English page 7 -- English page 8. You ask: "Mr. Delimustafic, the special unit had gone out to carry out several operations. There was dissatisfaction in those Serb villages. Vito Zepinic co-ordinated them. They split up following an agreement. They went to their F building. The conflict erupted and the killing of two special policemen and the wounding of three ensued. There were no wounded, nothing, on the other side." "Who do you hold responsible for the killings at Vraca?" And then it goes on somewhere. The Accused Mandic says: "I will rephrase the question. Mr. Delimustafic, do you know -- do you have any information that I, as your assistant at that moment, was involved in any way in the conflict at Vraca?" And Delimustafic answers: "I do not have such information, but by virtue of his office, the director of the school and member of the collegium, Balic, was responsible for everything that was going on at Vraca." Is that how it went?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the indictment alleged that I was responsible for the conflict at Vraca - that's the allegation of the prosecution of Bosnia-Herzegovina - and Mr. Delimustafic claimed that Mr. Balic, the director of the centre, without the knowledge of the Presidency or the Ministerial Collegium, had armed the men and prepared the defence to attack the Serbian police, who were just going into their own building, according to a prior agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who exactly was at the Vraca School at that moment?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was over the weekend, the second day of the Bajram holiday. Four hundred students were supposed to go home on leave. Those were young men between 15 and 18 years old. Director Balic had forbidden them to take this home leave. There were 180 trainees of that police course -- sorry, 170, and these trainees were the men who had come from Croatia or from Draska [phoen] area in Serbia who had gone through military training already, they were trained. And there were some instructors, mainly Muslim, because it was the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation why he had forbidden those students to take home leave on their holiday?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were hostages in this conflict between Serb members of the special unit and those trainees who had ambushed them. They had locked them up downstairs and held them as hostages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whom exactly did Director Balic arm?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a letter, and a commission had been set up. It was discussed in the Bruno Stojic case. Just before that event, the school had received three and a half million rounds, 7.62 millimetres, 600 rifles, and around 10 M-84 machine-guns, and I can tell you positively that these are not things that you need for training. And I ask Delimustafic to set up a commission to see why so many trainees had been sent to Vraca, to that school, and why this equipment was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did he give weapons to all these trainees? Whom did he arm?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said already trainees of all ethnicity were locked up there as hostages. And as for the defence of the school, aimed to protect the Serb special unit members from entering the school, that was provided by 100-something Muslim -- exclusively Muslim trainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how many members of the special unit were there who came to that school?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty-five.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Minister, was the media reporting correct that there was shooting also from Sandzak private houses behind Vraca?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The men who had been killed, and I have the medical documentation in my file in Sarajevo, were shot in the back of the head from a place called Sanac [phoen], populated mainly by people who had come from Serbia but were of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that Vraca is an almost 100 per cent Serb settlement and Sanac is an irregular settlement behind Vraca?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was between Grbavica and that training centre, which is spread over a large area, and that settlement is closer to Lukavica and Trebevic; I mean Vraca. Vraca is a mainly Serbian settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We still need this page. Mr. Delimustafic says that he has no such information that you were involved, and then Judge Jukic says: "Who was able to move this special unit? Would the assistant minister be authorised ..." And he probably means you when he says "assistant minister"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then Mr. Delimustafic says: "No." And the judge asks: "Who was authorised, who had the authority?" And Mr. Delimustafic says: "The Presidency and the government had the authority. Following an agreement it was the Presidency and the government and the Ministerial Collegium." Is this Judge Jukic a Croat?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, first of all, I think that's irrelevant, and I hope it begins to highlight the problem with the path we've moved down. And with all respect, it's difficult to glean the distinction between reading it into the record and admitting it, and I think both are inappropriate, and continue to maintain that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I find, Mr. Karadzic, your question as to the ethnicity of the judge irrelevant. What is your next question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then we can disregard this, although none of this is irrelevant. The judge asks: "Did the accused, as assistant minister, have the authority to activate that unit?" And Delimustafic says: "No." And now we will abide by Mr. Tieger's objection, and I would like page 15 in Serbian, page 15 in English. Just one more passage and I'll be done with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues is asking a question here. I'll -- first of all, explain who Judge Rodrigues is and read this question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues is one of the ICTY Judges, one of two ICTY Judges who was assistant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not relevant. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, first of all, I don't think this is the right page in English. It could be the next one, then. I have it noted down as page 13, but, in any case, it's the next page in English. And we don't have the right page in Serbian. It should be 15. Your Excellency, with all due respect, I believe this goes to the credit of Judge Jukic and the foreign judges as well. That tribunal has foreigners on its staff, and it acquitted this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is that your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that so, Witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It doesn't matter who the judge is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you interpret this question by Judge Rodrigues, that begins with the words: "All right, one more question ..."?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues: "All right, another question. At one moment, you said that if the collegium decided so and if the assistant minister was authorised by the collegium, he had the authority to act on your behalf. Do you remember if Vitomir Zepinic was in charge of all matters related to the division of the special unit?" And Delimustafic answers: "Well, I think so." Judge Rodrigues says: "Okay. You heard or were informed of the events in the school in Vraca. Were you informed of these events?" Delimustafic says: "Well, I was." Judge Rodrigues says: "Who informed you?" And Delimustafic answers: "Vitomir Zepinic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the rest of this text, it is established that you were not a member of the SDS, that you were proposed to the SDS by Vitomir Zepinic, and even Delimustafic, to Rajko Dukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's another statement of yours. Just put your question. What is your question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this testimony -- or was it established in those proceedings that you were not a member of the SDS, that Delimustafic and Rajko [as interpreted] Zepinic had proposed you to the SDS, and that you acted on the instructions of the collegium?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that, and I can only repeat, Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I've made it clear I think that there is some objection to the limited practice that the Court indicated it would permit, but now the accused is straying beyond that, seeking broad-based -- alleged broad-based determinations by this Court. I hope it illustrates some of the problems associated with this particular practice, beyond the factors I raised earlier which involve the circumvention of 92 ter and so on. But this is not even within the limited exception that the Court announced it would permit the accused in asking -- in reading some of the questions posed to Mr. Delimustafic. Now, he's seeking conclusions about what the Court overall determined, and I hope we won't be going down that path.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree with you, as far as the last question is concerned, but I'd like to hear what Judge Robinson [sic] has to say. Sorry, Morrison. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Illustrates the dangers of identification evidence, if nothing else. For myself, I agree with you, Mr. Tieger. Dr. Karadzic, it's one thing to ask a question related to a document. It's another thing to read the document out wholesale, ask the witness to adopt it, and then, furthermore, ask them to draw conclusions based upon what other people thought, or might have thought, or might have said, or might have accepted. Apart from anything else, it's not evidence that we could conceivably take into account in determining the truth of the matter. So apart from any procedural defect, it's wasting your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, the evidence in the previous trial isn't evidence before us, and the fact that it has been read into the record does not make it evidence. This is an important thing. It doesn't make it evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise, I do apologise. I was under the impression or I was labouring under the misconception that I was a fast learner, but obviously I'm not. Can we now see 1D1373.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, we mentioned the first directive of Hasan Efendic, issued on the 12th of April, 1992, immediately after the signing of the cease-fire -- of the armistice between the three parties. And Ambassador Cutileiro, this is his second directive. Do we have a translation? No. Well, look at this. This is from the 29th of April. You don't have to read it out in extenso. Just tell us what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a duplicate of 21000, which has a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly inform us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order by the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in which he asks that all the barracks of the Yugoslav People's Army be blocked and that no materiel or personnel can leave them; also, that all roads leading to Serbia or other territories should be blocked and in order to prevent the pullout of the army from the barracks and from specific places. Under 4, combat activities should be launched, attacks on members of the Yugoslav People's Army. In other words, a war should be started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say "throughout the territory of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are perhaps not concentrated enough. That's exactly what I said in my first sentence, "throughout the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my answer, I immediately said, right at the outset, "throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a technical question. Why do we have two sets of documents in this English translation? Maybe just duplicates. Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D399, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 1D56 now, 1D56, to see what action was taken by the Ministry of the Interior, according to this order of the Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you interpret for us briefly what this telegram is?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is practically a reproduced order. The one that we saw a while ago, it is exactly the same order sent to the Centre of Security, to the SUP of Sarajevo, and to Public Security Services. So all the three orders that Hasan Efendic had sent to Territorial Defence units are now being sent by the minister, with the minister's signature, to the police. They are exactly the same orders. Let me not repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was in this way actually the police subsumed under the Territorial Defence Staff, placed under its control, in joint operations against the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All armed forces united in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I am referring, on the one hand, to the police, the reserve police force, and the regular police, and, on the other hand, the paramilitary units, the Patriotic League, and the Green Berets, which I have already said a couple of hours ago, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D400.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to take a look at another two documents, only, in connection with this topic, and then we should move on to a different topic. Can we now see 1D58, please. Can you zoom in on it, please. I don't know whether we have the Serbian version. If the other side does not, then we probably don't have it either. Let me then summarise it. In English: [In English] "... main governing body of Islamic Association of Croatia and Slovenia, Zagreb," and so on and so on. "Acknowledgment of money received." Text: "We, members of the Emergency Commission on behalf of the Muslims of the Republic of Croatia for the assistance of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, hereby certify that we have received from the Honourable Kemal Seraj Eddine [phoen] and Dr. Fatih El Hassenein [phoen], the amount of US $300.000, commanded [sic] for the purchase of weapons to be dispatched to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. "The weapons will be purchased through the Finance Ministry of the Croatian Defence Ministry which had entered into agreement with the Bosnian government to that effect." Receipt verified by Sheik Shrowki Omar Yelshinsen [phoen]. [Interpretation] Let us see the date. It's the 4th of April, 1992 -- actually, it is the 29th of April, 1992. It is -- on the right-hand side, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this proof that the Islamic Community of Slovenia and Croatia, through Fatih El Hassanein, and others from Arab countries, procured weapons for Bosnia-Herzegovina in this early stage of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think this is calling for, I assume not on its face, request for information that this witness might possess, but, in fact, requests this witness offer or some sort of assessment about a document that he may never and presumably did not see before, and about which I have some objections anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without speculating on this matter, can you say what this document is or do you know, Mr. Mandic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true, Your Honours, this is the first time I see this document, but I now - and I also said so yesterday - through the Mesihat, the mosques in Zagreb, in Croatia, procured weapons for the Bosnian Muslims and then shared training for Bosnian Muslims in both Croatia and in Arabic countries. I've already spoken about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But have you no clue whether this is a genuine document or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see for the first time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: For the Bosnian Muslims, the Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karadzic, what is your next question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect for distinguished Mr. Tieger, my question was:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Mr. Srebrenkovic, who was imposed on you instead of Selimovic, the personnel officer, did he come from this Islamic Community?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was working in the Mesihat of this Islamic Community then, and he is working there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this document, the heading of which says "The Mesihat of the Islamic Community," is that association?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the religious community that I was testifying to in my statement yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have this document admitted? There will be a lot more to be said about the relief organisation and El Hassanein, and all the other aid and relief organisations that actually procured weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there's nothing about the document that -- there's no stamp, there's no -- we don't have the original to compare the translation to, so it's difficult for us in any way to assess its authenticity. So without more information, it's, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification, until we are satisfied as to its foundation?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, and I accept the possibility that further information may be adduced during the course of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, generally, it doesn't seem to me that there's likely to be much dispute as to the fact that weapons were purchased and distributed to, for wont of a better expression, Muslim forces. Isn't this something that could be the subject of agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, Your Honour, I agree that on its face, it seems that this is a matter that shouldn't be consuming as much court time as it is. So under -- while -- based on that, I would be inclined to agree I have found, over time, that efforts to reach such agreements founder on a number of particulars. We're happy to consider ways in which this issue can be short-cut in some manner and consume less court time. And, you're right, the extent to which this issue is in controversy is considerably less than would appear to be, based on the amount of time we seem to be spending on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask to zoom out of this document so that we can see the number under which this document came to be included in the file. As a matter of fact, it is at part of a police investigation on arms smuggling. You can see that. We can see the number under which this document was filed. We found it here, in fact. We didn't bring it here ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, but you are not giving evidence, and the witness has no clue as to that idea. So we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D401, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should just like to remind you that the date is the same as the one given by Hasan Efendic. With the leave and understanding of Mr. Tieger, can I offer a document that we have -- that is connected to this one and to the persons referred to by Mr. Mandic? But it would have to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's see what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the Crisis Staff of the Islamic Community of Croatia and Slovenia, of the 10th of April; the Crisis Staff. I believe that the witness cannot be aware of every single document, but he can be aware of practices, of developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I can read it, or can you read it, please?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Crisis Staff of the Islamic Community of Croatia and Slovenia, Zagreb. 10th April 1992." "Receipt, whereby I confirm that I, Djevdad Tinic [phoen] from Zagreb, have taken over from the Crisis Staff of the Islamic Community the following: "Automatic rifle, five pieces. "Sniper rifle, Stajer, 35. "Sniper rifle, Brno, no bullets. "Sniper rifle, Brno, no bullets. "Ammunition, 320 rounds ..."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we just scroll it a bit up so that we can see the signatures and the persons who feature in this document, or, rather, in this transaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you read their names out?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Goods taken over by Djevdad Tinic. "Goods taken over by Mirsad Srebrenkovic. "Goods handed over by Sefko Omerbasic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of this Sefko Omerbasic?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this Mirsad Srebrenkovic, he is our own personnel officer from the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there a date on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the 10th of April, Your Honours. It is in the top left corner.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the document is self-explanatory. Can you accept that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I noted the ERN number of this document. Can you scroll down to see the bottom of the page? Is that an ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What would you say to this document, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The ERN number is far from dispositive, although it might give us an opportunity to independently identify the provenance of the document. But I wasn't going to object, irrespective of the presence of the ERN number or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D402, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just one more document from this phase and this topic. Can we have 1D1414. [In English] The ERN there is 1414.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, let me ask you: All of these orders and these actions, primarily of Hasan Efendic, and then taken over from the MUP and so on and so forth, naturally resulted in what happened on the 2nd and 3rd of May in Sarajevo, when the army was slaughtered, soldiers who were withdrawing from Sarajevo who were slaughtered?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, inter alia, the answer is, Yes. However, the order to fire, or, rather, to use all available fire-arms against the convoy that was moving down Dobrovoljacka Street, from the Bistrik neighbourhood towards Grbavica and Vraca, was issued by Ejub Ganic. I heard it myself. That is when about 20 young men, age 19 to 21, were killed. They were military conscripts, doing their regular military service. They worked at the command and the communications centre there, and they were going home unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This evacuation of the Command of the 4th Military District, had that been agreed upon with Izetbegovic and General MacKenzie, UNPROFOR commander for Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an agreement between Mr. Izetbegovic and MacKenzie and the commander of that district, Milutin Kukanjac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. 271 in Serbian, please, and in English let's try to find our way. I hope that we manage to find our way in English as well. Perhaps it might be the next page in English. What we have here is 257 and then 271. Yes, this is 271, and in English it's the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Minister, you see Delimustafic here, who received that telegram and had to forward it, but he has his own opinion in that regard. Can you read out what Mr. Delimustafic is saying to the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, what is highlighted here?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Delimustafic says that Avdo Hebib sent this identical order on his behalf, unauthorised, and that is what had been done by Hasan Efendic. You see what he says here: "Without me knowing about it, he declared war." Delimustafic says that he asked Avdo Hebib to make a statement in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please read all of this out to us?

utterances.speaker: MOMCILO MANDIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Delimustafic: "Both we and his ministry made mistakes, like what Bakir did or like Avdo Hebib, what he did, when he ordered the war to start, people to open fire, occupy barracks. He sent an order to all centres without my knowledge. He declared war. I told him to make a statement in order to observe proper form. He never came to see me again. He doesn't speak to me anymore." Izetbegovic is asking Delimustafic: "Who did that?" Delimustafic: "Avdo Hebib." Izetbegovic is asking: "What did he do?" Delimustafic: "He declared war on the army. Four points. Signed the dispatch." Izetbegovic: "In what capacity?" Kljujic: "We have finished the recording. Don't record this."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
